observations.audio: The exact --image surface rejected WAV before provider submission with the documented image-format error. --expand-file-mentions exited successfully but sent neither audio bytes nor the 440HZ_250MS marker, so it is text mention expansion rather than native audio input.
observations.compaction: Not attempted: the exact client exposes threshold configuration but no public force-compaction action, and this intentionally small capture remained below its threshold.
observations.document: The exact --image surface rejected PDF before provider submission with the documented image-format error. --expand-file-mentions exited successfully but sent neither PDF bytes nor the ORBIT_2048 marker, so it is not a native document attachment surface.
observations.readable_reasoning: Not attempted: the credential-free response emitted no reasoning item, and Muse 0.2.1 exposes no separate public readable-thinking input surface.
observations.text: Three successful exact-client turns retain task, image-analysis, and recall text, including SM_CORPUS_7319, COPPER_4821, and BLUE_TRIANGLE_7319.
observations.tool_call: The exact client invoked its declared native read_file tool three times through the model response surface with stable call ids.
observations.tool_result: The durable log retains two successful file reads and the exact failed result text for missing-corpus-file.txt; Muse 0.2.1 does not store a separate error boolean on this result shape.
observations.tool_result_image: Not attempted: the exercised native read_file tool returns text only, and the pinned public CLI exposes no tool-result image injection surface.
observations.user_image: The exact repeatable --image surface accepted PNG and sent an image/png data URL to the provider. The durable log retains the prompt and model analysis but not the image bytes, so source portability is explicitly lossy.
observations.video: The exact --image surface rejected MP4 before provider submission with the documented image-format error. --expand-file-mentions exited successfully but sent neither video bytes nor the BLUE_TO_LIME_1S marker, so it is not a native video input surface.
